source_evidence.finding: Discovers only recipe directories whose notebook.ipynb exists in the checked-out tree and validates their names.
Uses git diff --name-only --no-renames with a three-dot comparison by default and fails on unreadable diffs.
source_evidence.excerpt:
def changed_paths(root: Path, base: str, head: str, dots: str = "...") -> list[str]:
    result = subprocess.run(
        [
            "git",
            "-C",
            str(root),
            "diff",
            "--name-only",
            "--no-renames",
            "-z",
            f"{base}{dots}{head}",
        ],
        capture_output=True,
        check=False,
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise SystemExit(f"git diff {base}{dots}{head} failed: {result.stderr.decode()[:300]}")
    return [p.decode("utf-8", "surrogateescape") for p in result.stdout.split(b"\0") if p]

          elif [ "$EVENT" = "push" ]; then

            python tools/notebook_ci.py matrix --base HEAD^ --head HEAD --lenient --github-output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  execute:
    name: Notebook (${{ matrix.recipe }})
    needs: discover
    if: needs.discover.outputs.count != '0'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      # A full run (push to main, the weekly cron, or a foundation change) can select every recipe
      # at once; without a cap this one job claims as many of the organisation's concurrent-job
      # slots as there are recipes, starving CI's other workflows and jobs. 10 keeps a wave a
      # deliberate, bounded choice (see "Run time and scaling" in docs/notebook-ci.md) rather than
      # whatever the organisation's own limit happens to be, and a pull request (at most one recipe
      # folder changed, ordinarily) never notices it.
      max-parallel: 10
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.discover.outputs.matrix) }}
    env:
      RECIPE: ${{ matrix.recipe }}

source_evidence.excerpt:
Until all four are observed for a given change, the allowlist is enforced by review only, exactly
as before any of this ran: a reviewer rejects a `.github/` or out-of-scope change in a recipe pull
request by hand, the same backstop named above for the allowlist generally.

## Which notebooks run

`python tools/notebook_ci.py matrix` lists the folders with a `notebook.ipynb`, `_template`
included. Planned catalog entries without a notebook add no matrix job, in either the original
track (01–60) or the multimodal track (61–100).

- **A push to `main`** runs the recipe folders changed since the previous tip of `main`
  (`github.event.before`) when the push touches nothing outside `recipes/<folder>/` and `README.md`
  (a recipe merge runs one notebook). It runs every notebook when anything else changed (shared
  code, tools, workflows, docs, the constraints file, anything a recipe reads). The diff is
  two-dot (`before..after`, the two trees). **A forced push is not trusted to say what changed**:
  GitHub sends the old tip as `before` (not zeros) and a three-dot diff would start from the merge
  base, so a rewound `main` selects nothing and a rewritten one selects the wrong folders. The
  workflow therefore runs every notebook when `github.event.forced` is true, and
  `matrix --push` also falls back to every notebook when `before` is not a commit in the clone (a
  first push) or is not an ancestor of the new tip (a rewind or a rewrite that `forced` somehow did
  not flag). `tests/test_notebook_ci_gates.py` pins a rewound and a rewritten `before`.
- **A weekly scheduled run** (Mondays, 04:17 UTC, on the default branch) runs every notebook. It
  exists so that a `main` run that was skipped, cancelled or lost, whose recipes the push selection
  would never revisit, is found within a week.
- **A manual run** (`workflow_dispatch`) has a `full` input. Left true (the default) it runs every
  notebook; false runs the recipe folders changed by the latest commit, by the same rule.
- **A pull request** runs only the recipe folders it changes, provided every changed path is inside
  a `recipes/<folder>/` or is exactly `README.md`. A recipe pull request is limited to that by the
  scope check, so one recipe's pull request does not re-run every published notebook.
- A pull request that changes anything else (shared code, tools, docs, workflows, the template's
  neighbours) runs every notebook, because shared code can change any recipe's result. **That
  includes a docs-only foundation pull request**: any path outside `recipes/` and `README.md`
  selects every notebook, `docs/**` included. This is an accepted cost (see "Run time and scaling"),
  because telling which documents a notebook reads would be a second source of truth to maintain.
- A change that only regenerates `README.md` runs none, and `Notebooks (execute)` is green.

Runs on `main` are never cancelled or replaced by a newer push (each push has its own concurrency

existing_decision.body:
Governance reconciliation at exact main `bad1bf2997a7e8f0811d5b9719dd9fb6643efbdb`: preserve the current conditional matrix contract. Do not add an unconditional non-empty-matrix requirement.

The opening example does not currently demonstrate a missing execution:

- If content is already present at the merge base, that notebook is not changed by the PR's three-dot diff. The proposed “diff touches notebook” assertion would not fire on that example either.
- For a changed recipe notebook still present at the head, `notebook_ci.select` adds its recipe and intersects with the notebooks present at that head. The existing generated-README-plus-notebook test explicitly expects that recipe to be selected.
- Deleting a notebook intentionally selects no notebook to execute. The existing deletion test pins that behavior. A raw “touches notebook” rule would incorrectly reject this documented case.
- The stable `Notebooks (execute)` job checks discovery success and requires execute success when the count is nonzero; at zero it requires execute to be skipped. The merge gate also needs to verify the expected matrix for the actual head/base, not infer completeness from whichever check names happen to exist.

Source locations: `tools/notebook_ci.py::select`, `tests/test_notebook_ci_gates.py::test_recipe_pull_request_with_the_generated_readme_still_selects_only_its_recipe`, `test_deleting_a_recipe_notebook_selects_nothing_to_run`, and the aggregate job in `.github/workflows/notebooks.yml`. This is a source/contract reconciliation, not a newly executed reproducer.

The routine disposition is to treat the stated scenario as unproven, rather than a new human policy question or a blocking defect in every empty matrix. The primary can close that defect claim with this evidence. If a concrete head/base pair omits a changed notebook that still exists at the head, retain it as a reproducible selection defect. Any separately proposed defense-in-depth invariant must check the expected recipe identities, exclude intentional deletions, and prove failure on an actually missing selection; a nonzero count alone would not establish coverage.
existing_decision.interpretation: Retain the conditional matrix contract; primary may close the stated unproven claim. A real changed-present-notebook omission would require a concrete head/base reproducer. No new policy question is needed.

PREPARED — NOT POSTED

Triage reconciliation at exact current main `2dd687f858549ee8eeb9c98f83344814dfc7d0b6` supports closing the original defect claim as unproven under the existing decision in https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/issues/284#issuecomment-6186880768. No implementation change is proposed by this disposition.

The current source preserves the documented conditional matrix contract:

- `tools/notebook_ci.py::select` collects the changed recipe identities and intersects them with notebooks present in the checked-out tree. A root `README.md` change does not remove a changed notebook's selection. The existing `test_recipe_pull_request_with_the_generated_readme_still_selects_only_its_recipe` modifies the notebook and generated README together and asserts the exact recipe identity.
- `test_deleting_a_recipe_notebook_selects_nothing_to_run` explicitly asserts an empty selection after notebook deletion. A blanket rule requiring a nonempty matrix whenever the diff mentions a notebook would reject this intentional case.
- `.github/workflows/notebooks.yml` keeps `Notebooks (execute)` as an always-running aggregate. It requires discovery success; with count zero it requires execute to be skipped; with any other count it requires execute success. It does not treat an unsuccessful selected execution as a pass.
- Content already present at the merge base is not a changed notebook in that three-dot comparison. The opening example therefore does not demonstrate an omitted changed notebook, and its proposed diff-based assertion would not fire on that example either.
